questions.stem: Why does every submission meet this criterion?

options.text: The ward hires only competent nurses
All nurses are equally skilled
Roster membership is a precondition, not a performance
Markers are lenient on roster checks

questions.explanation: Roster membership is a precondition everyone satisfies. The tempting wrong idea calls it leniency.
questions.hint: Check whether the criterion distinguishes performances.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: What a set of weightings rewards
questions.learningObjective: Explain what a weighting scheme rewards
questions.stem: Handover weightings give fifty percent to accuracy and fifty to empathy; what does this reward?

options.text: Speed of completion
Accuracy alone
Empathy alone
Balanced performance across accuracy and empathy

questions.explanation: Equal weights reward balance across both. The tempting wrong idea privileges one component.
questions.hint: Equal weights mean neither dominates.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Self-assessment without a shared reference point
questions.learningObjective: Identify the flaw in self-assessment without a reference
questions.stem: A nurse self-assesses handover skill with no rubric and no peer comparison; what goes wrong?

answer.exemplar: Without a rubric or peer comparison, the self-assessment rests on private standards, so scores cannot be calibrated or trusted.

questions.explanation: Private standards prevent calibration. The tempting wrong idea blames the nurse's honesty alone.
questions.hint: Ask what the score is measured against.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Scores that follow a relationship rather than a text
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish scores tied to relationships from text evidence
questions.stem: Handover scores rise for nurses who smile at the marker; the notes are identical; what do scores follow?

options.text: The quality of the notes
The social relationship, not the notes
The length of the handover
The time of day

questions.explanation: Identical notes with varying scores follow the social relationship. The tempting wrong idea trusts the notes.
questions.hint: Hold the text constant and see what varies.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: A grade and the reason attached to it
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a grade needs an attached reason
questions.stem: A fail grade is given with the reason 'unclear'; why is that still insufficient?

options.text: One word is too short for any rubric
The grade should be higher
It does not say which part is unclear or how to fix it
The marker should have passed the student

questions.explanation: 'Unclear' names a fault but not where or how to fix. The tempting wrong idea blames length or verdict.
questions.hint: Ask what the learner can act on.

questions.topic: A comment that tells the student what to do next
questions.learningObjective: Identify a comment that gives actionable next steps
questions.stem: Which handover comment tells the student what to do next?

options.text: Refer to the rubric
Your handover missed the recommendation
options.misconception: names a fault but no action

options.text: Good handover overall
Your handover missed the recommendation; add it in one sentence

questions.explanation: The actionable comment states the fault and the next step. The tempting wrong idea stops at naming the fault.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Feedback that arrives after the assessed work is closed
questions.learningObjective: Identify feedback given after the work is closed

stimulus.body: Feedback on a handover arrives after the placement ends and the grade is final. The student cannot revise the assessed handover.

It informs future placements only
It replaces the rubric next time
It proves the marker was fair

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: What a revision memo has to carry
questions.learningObjective: State what a revision memo must carry
questions.stem: A revision memo for a handover must carry what changed, why, and the new version; what is its purpose?

answer.exemplar: Its purpose is to make the change trail transparent so the marker can see what was revised and why, not just the final text.

questions.explanation: The memo makes the change trail transparent. The tempting wrong idea treats it as a resubmission of final text.
questions.hint: The reader needs the trail, not just the result.

questions.topic: What a piece of a portfolio actually evidences

Growth across the placement

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: A thesis that can be tested and one that cannot
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a testable thesis from an untestable one

stimulus.body: Thesis P: structured handover reduces omitted information by fifteen percent. Thesis Q: handover embodies professional respect. Both are proposed for an essay.

questions.stem: Which thesis can be tested?

options.text: Neither, because essays are subjective
Thesis Q, because it names a value
Both, because both are arguable
Thesis P, because it states a measurable claim

questions.explanation: A measurable claim can be tested; a value claim cannot. The tempting wrong idea treats arguability as testability.
questions.hint: Ask what evidence could confirm or refute it.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Whether a source fits the claim being made
questions.learningObjective: Judge whether a source fits the claim
questions.stem: A source on emergency handover is cited for a routine clinic claim; does it fit?

answer.exemplar: It does not fit unless the claim is generalised across urgency levels; the context mismatch means the source supports a narrower claim.

questions.explanation: A context mismatch narrows the supported claim. The tempting wrong idea assumes any handover source fits any claim.
questions.hint: Check the setting the source studied.
